title: Quiet stretch, chat_active gap, and fresh-session boundary scenario
description: Same synthetic clock convention (seconds after start). Focused on a quiet period, a chat_active gap where turn_busy is false, and the same/fresh history difference. Invented data only.
assumptions: turn_busy (busy_interval) and chat_active (chat_interval) are separate supplied facts; chat_interval extends past the turn so autonomous opportunities during the gap target the placement rule, not a finished response.

policies.label: fixed interval
policies.assumptions: Fixed opportunities every 300 seconds, starting at zero; placement controls execution.

policies.label: explicitly seeded/listed jittered interval
policies.assumptions: Every 300 seconds plus the listed repeating offset array; not random samples.

policies.label: event driven
policies.assumptions: Supplied human, ambient and memory arrivals propose autonomous opportunities, independently of the ordinary human reply loop. Internal outputs do not trigger themselves.

policies.label: self-scheduled one-shots
policies.assumptions: Only fixture self-wake plans; consumed once.

policies.label: idle-window trigger
policies.assumptions: One opportunity after a complete quiet observation window; sampled at fixture ticks. No inference about sleep, mood, or contact need.

policies.label: hybrid timer/event/self-wake
policies.assumptions: Ticks + events + self-wake as raw candidates; coalescing owned by placement.

placements.label: main_skip
placements.assumptions: LAB CHOICE. Skip autonomous opportunities during chat_active.

placements.label: main_defer
placements.assumptions: LAB CHOICE. Coalesce and rebuild after chat_active ends.

placements.label: independent
placements.assumptions: LAB CHOICE. Run in a separate autonomous session during chat_active; no main writes.

timeline.note: chat_active spans past the turn: 1500-1800 has turn_busy=false but chat_active=true
